title: No finite rulebook can certify every safe program: an impossibility theorem for gatekeeping AI agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.13367v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: An AI assistant writes small programs, and a gatekeeper must decide, from the code alone, whether each one may run. Suppose the rules are fixed: never perform a forbidden action, never let the output depend on a secret, always answer eventually. Can two rulebooks, one listing what is allowed and one listing what is not, both be complete, if every rule must be backed by evidence that a machine can check in finite time? We prove that they cannot. Checkable evidence can only establish what a finite record settles, and ``never'' and ``eventually'' are never settled by a finite record. For prohibitions the failure is one-sided: every violation can be caught by watching, but no safe program can be cleared for good. For confidentiality and responsiveness, neither side can be. We characterise exactly which rules about visible behaviour evidence can confirm, and we show that any sound rulebook of $n$ bits omits a compliant program of about $n$ bi

translated_title: 没有任何有限规则手册能够认证所有安全程序：AI代理把关的不可能性定理
translated_abstract: 一个AI助手编写小程序，而把关者必须仅凭代码决定每个程序能否运行。假设规则是固定的：绝不执行被禁止的操作、绝不让输出依赖于秘密、最终总要给出回答。若每条规则都必须有机器能在有限时间内检验的证据支持，那么两本规则手册——一本列出允许的内容、一本列出禁止的内容——能否同时做到完备？我们证明它们不能。可检验的证据只能确立有限记录所能确定的事情，而“从不”与“最终”永远不会被有限记录所确定。对于禁止性规则，失败是单方面的：每一次违规都可以通过监视被发现，但没有任何安全程序能够被永久放行；而对于保密性和响应性，双方都无法判定。我们精确刻画了证据究竟能够确认哪些关于可见行为的规则，并证明任何n比特的可靠规则手册都会遗漏一个大约n比特的合规程序。
tldr: 本文证明了一个不可能性定理：由于机器可检验的证据只能确认有限记录所能确定的内容，而“从不”与“最终”类性质无法被有限记录确定，因此不存在完备的有限规则手册能认证所有安全程序——禁止性规则只能单向地发现违规却无法永久放行安全程序，保密性与响应性规则则连违规都无法可靠判定。
en_tdlr: This paper proves an impossibility theorem: since machine-checkable evidence can only settle what a finite record settles, and "never" and "eventually" are never settled by finite records, no finite rulebook can completely certify all safe programs—prohibitions can only catch violations one-sidedly without ever clearing safe programs for good, while confidentiality and responsiveness rules cannot be decided in either direction.
